def: A function that runs on a GPU, launched across many parallel workers at once.
A Python-embedded language for GPU kernels in which each program handles a block of data and the compiler maps it to threads.
One copy of a Triton kernel, identified by its program id, that processes one block of the data.
A boolean vector that switches off the lanes of a block that fall past the end of the data.
A benchmark of 250 PyTorch workloads in which a model must write GPU kernels that are correct and faster.
The fraction of tasks whose generated kernel is correct and more than p times faster than the reference.
The least possible run time, the larger of the time to do the arithmetic and the time to move the data at the hardware's peak rates.
Limited by arithmetic throughput rather than by moving data.
A timing hack that runs the work on a separate CUDA stream so the timer does not see it.
A revision of KernelBench with a TF32 baseline and a hidden test suite over four input distributions.
